verdict.rationale: Auth0's own docs show it implements standard OAuth 2.0 flows for developers, including Client Credentials and the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization flow. It also offers API protection with OAuth 2.0, hosted Universal Login and per-app-type quickstarts. Community reports of integrating in days support that protocol details need not be hand-rolled. However, the specific flows the story names are not evidenced. missing for 10: explicit documentation of authorization code with PKCE, refresh-token issuance/rotation for Auth0-issued tokens, OIDC conformance details, SDK-level evidence of abstracting these flows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can implement standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows (authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens) without hand-rolling protocol details

citations.quote: You built an API and you want to secure it with OAuth 2.0.
device apps use the Device Authorization Flow (ratified in OAuth 2.0), in which they pass along their Client ID to initiate the authorization process and get a token.
This flow is best suited for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications, such as CLIs, daemons, or backend services
To get up and running swiftly, choose your application type for a step-by-step quickstart tutorial.
